topic: MemCompiler persistent-memory identity erasure at the receiver retrieval boundary

facts: Persistent task memory is backed by Chroma main_memory.
add_memory creates a Document from task_main plus MASMessage metadata and calls main_memory.add_documents without supplying an explicit application-level record ID.
_retrieve_memory_raw obtains Document objects from similarity search, then converts only doc.metadata into MASMessage via MASMessage.from_dict before returning successful and failed task messages.
retrieve_memory reranks and returns MASMessage lists and insight strings; no Chroma document ID is carried through this API.
memory_size reads main_memory.get()['ids'], demonstrating that persistent backend IDs do exist even though the retrieval API discards them before the receiver boundary.
MASMessage contains task_main, task_description, task_trajectory, label, chain_of_states and extra_fields.
MASMessage.to_dict/from_dict serialize those semantic fields but contain no persistent storage-record identifier.

scope_limited_findings.claim: The current public MemCompiler backend has persistent Chroma record IDs, but the receiver-facing retrieval boundary erases them: retrieved Documents are converted from metadata into MASMessage values and returned without the backend ID. Therefore a downstream trajectory cannot prove that two conditions received the same persistent memory record merely because they received semantically similar or equal text.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Current public revision ec5a579... implementation only; not attribution of historical evaluated run internals.

scope_limited_findings.claim: A digest of the returned MASMessage can prove equality of receiver-visible returned content, but it is weaker than exact persistent-record lineage when the store could contain duplicate/equivalent records. Same-content and same-backend-record are distinct provenance tiers.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Provenance semantics; does not assert duplicate records existed in the reported benchmark.

scope_limited_findings.claim: Exact receiver-memory provenance is instrumentable without changing model behavior: collect the backend record ID and canonical content digest as a read-only sidecar at retrieval time, while preserving the existing MASMessage values and prompt bytes passed to the compiler/executor.
scope_limited_findings.scope: Future-run instrumentation design from the current public retrieval architecture; not a claim that upstream has implemented it.

protocol_relation.rule: Never upgrade a content-equality claim to persistent-record identity without stable backend IDs or an equivalent collision-resistant application-level identity bound before the Document-to-MASMessage conversion.

next_actions: Specify a zero-behavior-change ScienceWorld evaluation sidecar that binds pre/post memory snapshots, update policy, ordered retrieval output identities/digests and candidate-pool digest.
Search for a public Table-3 bridge artifact containing a memory database snapshot or stable retrieval identities.
If future instrumentation cannot expose backend IDs without changing retrieval behavior, retain the weaker same-content claim tier instead of asserting same persistent record.
